extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians, comedy writers, and performers working on stagecraft
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for creating and judging act-outs — the moment a comedian shifts from narration to dramatized embodiment — focusing on commitment, specificity, emotional choice, and 'show don't tell' technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: You Don't Need a Perfect Impression
rubrics_metrics.description: You don't have to be a great actor or do a perfect impression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can deliver a line in your own voice and still get solid laughs. An act out isn't always an impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Fully commit to the emotions, punchlines, choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Half-hearted acting won't sell the performance. Correct commitment is key to credibility on stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show, Don't Tell
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever you have an opportunity to introduce information, show, don't tell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showing brings the audience into the present moment — urgent and alive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Specific with Characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the 'ghost mannequin' — a vague imaginary character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the character qualities, characteristics, identity. Specificity adds dynamic and dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional Variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiment with different emotional filters for the same line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record yourself saying lines with many emotions. Sometimes confusion lands harder than surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there a clear shift from narration to embodiment?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the performance clearly move from telling the story to physically/visually enacting it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A distinct mode shift (narration → embodied performance) creates surprise and makes the act-out register as an incongruity for the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the character/voice specific (not a ghost mannequin)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the acted character or voice given concrete qualities and identity rather than being vague?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific details about the character provide dynamics and dimensions; avoid indistinct or generic portrayals that fail to engage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the comic fully committed?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the performer fully inhabit the emotional and physical choices of the act-out?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full commitment sells the performance; half-hearted acting undermines credibility and reduces laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the act-out show rather than tell?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the act-out introduce information through behavior and embodiment instead of exposition?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showing pulls the audience into the present moment and makes the bit feel urgent and alive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the emotional choice the funniest available?
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the performer selected the emotional tone that maximizes comedic impact for the line?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try multiple emotional filters — record alternatives. Sometimes unexpected emotions (e.g., confusion) land better than obvious choices (e.g., surprise).
